cards.method: Market-based systemic risk: CoVaR / Delta-CoVaR (Adrian-Brunnermeier) + correlation-network measures
cards.when: a matrix of market returns (column 1 = the market/system index, columns 2. = the institutions); you want the contribution of each institution to systemic risk (CoVaR/Delta-CoVaR in the sense of Adrian-Brunnermeier, static or time-varying with state variables) or monthly correlation-network measures (degree/closeness/eigenvector centrality) + a system-wide index
cards.when_not: there is no market index in column 1; fewer than two institutions; you want the VaR or ES of a portfolio (-> #65), or a conditional Growth-at-Risk (-> #64); you want Diebold-Yilmaz spillover or FEVD connectedness (-> #51/#52, category 09); a quantile level other than 95%, which is hardcoded

alternatives.criterion: you want an unconditional CoVaR/Delta-CoVaR per institution — a single cross-sectional picture, without state variables
you want a conditional CoVaR/Delta-CoVaR that evolves with lagged macro-financial state variables (VIX/spreads) + the system-wide index Delta_CoVaR_t
you want the topology of the correlation network (centrality) + a systemic risk index (SR) per month, not a tail CoVaR
you want directional spillovers from an FEVD (to/from/net) rather than correlation-network centrality or a quantile CoVaR
you want the tail risk of ONE portfolio/series, not a cross-system contribution

output_key_fields: CoVaR_95 / CoVaR_50: the VaR of the system when institution i is at its VaR@95 / median (per institution)
Delta_CoVaR: the systemic contribution of institution i = CoVaR_95 - CoVaR_50 (an identity); loss-signed
CoVaR_i_q_t / Delta_CoVaR_i_q_t: time-varying matrices, (n-1) × institutions + dates
Delta_CoVaR_t: the system-wide index (the cross-sectional mean Delta-CoVaR times 100, where positive means higher risk); the first element is blank, an off-by-one
Degree/Closeness_Centrality/Eigenvector_Centrality: monthly network measures, min-max scaled to [0,1]
SR: the systemic risk index (a correlation-corrected realized portfolio volatility), min-max scaled to [0,1]
q=0.95, a hardcoded constant; n_institutions/n_state_variables/n_months/seed as the audit trail
network: it requires n_months>=3 (a post-gate, blocked-by-gate); ~>=100 daily rows — 90 rows give only 2 months, where the monthly min-max degenerates every measure to {0,1}
interpretation_traps: q=0.95 and q_50=0.5 ARE HARDCODED — the quantile level is NOT parameterisable (tau=0.05)
Delta_CoVaR = CoVaR_95 - CoVaR_50 EXACTLY; its sign follows the slope of the quantile regression (a positive co-movement with the market ⇒ Delta-CoVaR<0, a loss)
column 1 = the market/system index (the LHS), columns 2. = the institutions (the RHS) — NOT the other way round; the wrong order ⇒ a wrong CoVaR
the first Delta_CoVaR_t is structurally blank, an off-by-one at the first period — do not interpret it as 0
the network is fragile with few months, since the monthly sequence leaves gaps in the index; the gate requires at least 90 observations
the eigenvector centrality is non-deterministic at the 1e-18 level (the iterative eigensolver); the wrapper stabilises it by seeding the generator
a degenerate input (a constant column) gives a 'singular design matrix' error inside the quantile fit — a hard error, not a silent result
the VaR is computed parametrically (qnorm, assuming normality of the institution) — not as a historical/empirical quantile
sources: Adrian & Brunnermeier 2016 'CoVaR' American Economic Review 106(7) 1705-1741 (the definition of CoVaR/Delta-CoVaR)
Billio, Getmansky, Lo, Pelizzon 2012 'Econometric measures of connectedness and systemic risk' JFE 104(3) 535-559 (the correlation-network measures)
live introspection in the engine (an independent quantile-regression recomputation) — wrapper footer IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (c21_systemic_risk/market_systemic_risk)

cards.method: Financial-network contagion: DebtRank + Furfine cascades + interbank exposure-matrix reconstruction (Maximum Entropy / Minimum Density)
cards.when: a bilateral network of financial exposures (interbank/counterparty): (a) only the MARGINS are KNOWN (assets per node + liabilities per node) → reconstruct the n×n exposure matrix with Maximum Entropy (dense) or Minimum Density (sparse, realistic); (b) the exposure matrix + capital buffers are KNOWN → measure systemic risk/contagion with DebtRank (continuous stress) or traditional default cascades (a Furfine threshold), identifying the most systemic nodes (too-central-to-fail)
cards.when_not: non-financial networks, or general centrality and community work (-> #55); spillover or connectedness from a VAR and its FEVD of returns (-> #51/#52); you want the tail risk of one series (VaR and ES, #65; Growth-at-Risk, #64); you have only indicators and no network; Bayesian Erdős-Rényi sampling of a network from its margins (-> #223)

alternatives.criterion: you want a fully connected (dense) matrix that maximises entropy subject to the margins; deterministic; it understates concentration/contagion (a known issue: much denser than real interbank networks)
you want a SPARSE, more realistic matrix (few large exposures, Anand et al. 2015); STOCHASTIC → a seed is mandatory for reproducibility
you want a CONTINUOUS measure of systemic importance — how much stress the failure of each node transmits (Bardoscia et al. 2015); single_hit=True selects the older Battiston 2012 variant
you want discrete default cascades (which nodes default in a chain when the losses exceed the buffer), not continuous stress
you want a Bayesian posterior distribution of networks consistent with the margins (ER/Gibbs), not a single ME/MD point estimate
you want general centrality/community/connectivity, not contagion-specific DebtRank/cascade dynamics

output_key_fields: exposure_matrix (nrm_reconstruct_matrix): the reconstructed n×n exposure matrix (rows are lenders and assets, columns borrowers and liabilities; a registered handle for chaining into nrm_contagion)
density/n_links (nrm_reconstruct_matrix): the sparsity of the network (minimum density far below maximum entropy); total_exposure: the total volume
max_rowsum_resid/max_colsum_resid (nrm_reconstruct_matrix): how well the requested margins were honoured — the fit quality
seed (nrm_reconstruct_matrix): the seed that was used, critical for the minimum-density route
results (nrm_contagion): a frame per scenario — scenario/original_stress/additional_stress/original_losses/additional_losses/additional_defaults
additional_stress (nrm_contagion): the unweighted DebtRank of each node when every node is shocked; most_systemic_scenario names the most systemic node
total_additional_defaults (nrm_contagion): the total number of chain defaults beyond the initial shock
weights_defaulted (nrm_contagion): True when equal weights were used, the fallback when none were supplied
user weights in nrm_contagion: a hard gate requires their sum to be strictly positive; a zero sum would divide by zero and give a NaN systemic stress (blocked by the gate)
interpretation_traps: MATRIX ORIENTATION: rowsums=ASSETS (the creditor/lender per row), colsums=LIABILITIES (the debtor/borrower per column); M[i,j]>0 means an «assets network»: i holds a claim/asset on j (i lent to j). exposure_type='liabilities' REVERSES the convention — state correctly which one describes your matrix
BALANCE is mandatory: sum(rowsums)==sum(colsums) (total assets = total liabilities in a closed system); otherwise ME silently rescales the rowsums → a hard gate
MD (min_dens) is STOCHASTIC: a different seed → a different matrix/results; always record/pin the seed; ME/DebtRank/threshold are deterministic
additional_stress is NON-NEGATIVE additional stress (systemic amplification), NOT a z-score; ME understates transmission (too dense a network) — prefer MD for realistic exposures

shock: 'all' = one default scenario per node (a per-node DebtRank); a numeric vector = ONE scenario of a uniform proportional shock in [0,1]; values outside [0,1] are rejected (otherwise contagion silently returns a meaningless 0)
leaving the weights unset trips a bug in the raw routine; the wrapper works around it with equal weights (weights_defaulted=True) — supply total assets as weights for an economic weighting
single_hit=True (the older Battiston 2012 single-hit DebtRank) applies ONLY to method='debtrank'; with 'threshold' it is rejected
sources: Battiston, Puliga, Kaushik, Tasca & Caldarelli 2012 'DebtRank: Too Central to Fail?' Scientific Reports 2:541
Bardoscia, Battiston, Caccioli & Caldarelli 2015 'DebtRank: A Microscopic Foundation for Shock Propagation' PLoS ONE 10(6)
Upper & Worm 2004 'Estimating bilateral exposures in the German interbank market' European Economic Review 48, 827-849 (Maximum Entropy)
Anand, Craig & von Peter 2015 'Filling in the blanks: network structure and interbank contagion' Quantitative Finance 15(4), 625-636 (Minimum Density)
Furfine 2003 'Interbank Exposures: Quantifying the Risk of Contagion' JMCB 35(1) (threshold default cascades)
wrapper footer IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (c21_systemic_risk/financial_network_contagion)

cards.method: Bayesian interbank-network reconstruction (the Gandy-Veraart Gibbs sampler, an Erdős-Rényi hierarchical model)
cards.when: you know only the MARGINS of an interbank network — the row sums l (the total liabilities of each bank) & the column sums a (the total claims) — and you want to reconstruct the UNKNOWN n×n matrix of bilateral exposures L; Bayesian sampling of all the matrices consistent with the margins -> a posterior mean matrix, the probability of an edge per cell, the network density (an input for contagion/stress tests)
cards.when_not: you ALREADY have the full exposure matrix (go straight to contagion or centrality, category 09, #55/#51); you want network centrality or connectedness rather than reconstruction; non-square margins, or known cells (scoped out); a deterministic maximum-entropy or RAS reconstruction rather than a Bayesian posterior; margins that do not balance (a gate)

alternatives.criterion: you need a valid calibrated model BEFORE the sampler; you tune targetdensity (the expected share of existing edges)
you believe in a dense/interconnected network (a fully connected core); a smaller one -> a sparse network (few large exposures)
you want ONE point estimate (no posterior/uncertainty); it typically overstates interconnection (a fully connected bias) — Gandy-Veraart corrects that with sparsity
the exposure matrix is KNOWN and you want diffusion/centrality metrics, not a reconstruction

output_key_fields: mean_matrix: the n×n posterior MEAN exposure matrix (rowSums==l, colSums==a, a zero diagonal — guaranteed)
prob_link: the n×n posterior probability that an edge EXISTS, P(L[i,j]>0) ∈ [0,1]
sd_matrix / lower_matrix / upper_matrix: the uncertainty per cell (the standard deviation + the quantiles probs)
density: the mean network density (the share of positive off-diagonal edges)
out_degree / in_degree: the expected degree per bank (the sums of prob_link)
row_sum_max_dev / col_sum_max_dev: the maximum deviation from the margins (~0 = a sound reconstruction)
n_moving_cells: the cells that moved in the MCMC (the rest are deterministic/forced)

achieved_density (build_er_model): the REALIZED margin-conditional density (the mean off-diagonal link proportion over seeded sample_HierarchicalModel draws; the same quantity as the density of sample_interbank_network) — NOT the unconditional prior density of genL; directly comparable with targetdensity
model / samples: the raw handles (systemicrisk_er_model / systemicrisk_gv_samples) -> a to_mcp stub, registered for chaining
seed: the reproducibility seed (every stochastic path is seeded)
interpretation_traps: ORIENTATION: l = the row sums = the LIABILITIES (what bank i owes, row i), a = the column sums = the CLAIMS (what is owed to it, column j); L[i,j] = the exposure of i to j — do not transpose l/a; the post-gate rowSums==l & colSums==a catches it
sum(l) MUST equal sum(a) (total liabilities == total claims); a mismatch -> a hard gate 'they do not balance', NOT a silent adjustment

achieved_density can EXCEED targetdensity when the margins force a minimum number of edges (forced links); too LOW a targetdensity -> calibrate_ER ERRORS with 'Could not find feasible matrix', not a warning
both functions are STOCHASTIC (the calibration samples; the Gibbs sampler is MCMC); ALWAYS pass a seed for reproducibility — the same seed -> an identical posterior
the diagonal is always zero (no self-exposure); the diagonal of prob_link == 0
a small nsamples/thin -> a noisy estimate (the MCMC has not converged); raise them for production; the defaults (100/100) are conservative for small networks
mean_matrix is NOT the 'true' matrix — it is the posterior mean; the uncertainty lives in sd_matrix/lower/upper; use prob_link for the structure, not only the mean
sources: Gandy & Veraart 2017 'A Bayesian Methodology for Systemic Risk Assessment in Financial Networks' Management Science 63(12) 4428-4446
Gandy & Veraart 2019 'Adjustable Network Reconstruction with Applications to CDS Exposures' J. Multivariate Analysis 172 193-209
wrapper footer IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (c21_systemic_risk/market_systemic_riskisk)

cards.method: Marginal expected shortfall, SES and SRISK
cards.when: measuring how much an institution contributes to system-wide distress, and what capital it would need in a crisis
cards.when_not: the institution is unlisted so there is no equity series; the sample contains no stress episode to calibrate against

alternatives.criterion: the system's risk conditional on the institution
the institution's loss conditional on the system
the mechanism rather than the correlation

output_key_fields: mes: marginal expected shortfall in system tail events
srisk: expected capital shortfall in a crisis scenario
lrmes: long-run MES from the simulated dynamics
ranking: institutions ordered by contribution
interpretation_traps: SRISK IS DOMINATED BY SIZE AND LEVERAGE; ranking institutions by it largely reproduces a ranking by liabilities, which is informative but not the same as a risk measure
MES and CoVaR answer opposite conditional questions and routinely produce different rankings of the same institutions
the crisis scenario is an assumption (a market decline of a stated size), and the estimate scales with it
sources: Acharya, Pedersen, Philippon & Richardson 2017 (Review of Financial Studies 30:2-47)
Brownlees & Engle 2017 (Review of Financial Studies 30:48)
DOI 10.1093/rfs/hhw088

cards.method: Absorption ratio and principal-component systemic indicators
cards.when: a market-wide fragility indicator: when returns are explained by few factors, shocks propagate rather than diversify
cards.when_not: the cross-section is too small for the eigenvalue structure to be estimated; the panel is unbalanced

alternatives.criterion: the share of variance in the leading components
the whole spectrum rather than a share
you want a simpler summary

output_key_fields: absorption_ratio: variance share in the leading components
delta_ar: the standardised change, which is the signal
eigenvalues: the spectrum
centrality: institution contributions to the leading components
interpretation_traps: THE LEVEL OF THE ABSORPTION RATIO IS NOT COMPARABLE across different asset universes; only its CHANGE within one universe carries information
a rising ratio indicates fragility, not an imminent event -- it has led major drawdowns but also many non-events
the window length determines how fast the indicator moves and is a substantive choice
sources: Kritzman, Li, Page & Rigobon 2011 (Journal of Portfolio Management 37:112-126)
Billio, Getmansky, Lo & Pelizzon 2012 (Journal of Financial Economics 104:535)
scikit-learn

cards.when: mapping which institutions lead which, and summarising the resulting directed network as a systemic indicator
cards.when_not: the cross-section is large relative to the sample, where pairwise tests are dominated by multiple testing

alternatives.criterion: simple, but a severe multiplicity problem
many nodes, sparsity assumed
variance decompositions rather than tests

output_key_fields: adjacency: the estimated directed network
density: share of significant links, the headline indicator
centrality: in, out and eigenvector centrality per node
n_tests: the multiplicity the adjustment had to handle
interpretation_traps: PAIRWISE GRANGER TESTS ACROSS N INSTITUTIONS ARE N(N-1) HYPOTHESES; without multiplicity adjustment the network density is mostly false positives
Granger causality in returns is predictive lead-lag, not a causal or contagion mechanism, and the naming misleads readers persistently
network density rises mechanically with sample size because tests gain power, so time series of density must hold the window fixed
sources: Billio, Getmansky, Lo & Pelizzon 2012 (Journal of Financial Economics 104:535-559)
Diebold & Yilmaz 2014 (Journal of Econometrics 182:119)
networkx

cards.when: aggregating many market indicators into one stress measure, with time-varying correlation so the index rises when stress becomes systemic
cards.when_not: the component set is too narrow for an index to mean anything; the components are not available at a common frequency

alternatives.criterion: transparent, ignores correlation
correlation-weighted, rises when stress is broad
the leading factor across indicators

output_key_fields: index: the composite stress index
subindices: stress per market segment
correlation_contribution: how much time-varying correlation adds
components: the standardised inputs
interpretation_traps: CORRELATION-WEIGHTED AGGREGATION IS THE POINT: simultaneous stress across segments is systemic in a way that the same stress in one segment is not, and a simple average cannot express that
the transformation of raw indicators to a common scale -- cumulative distribution or standardisation -- changes the index level and its history
recursive standardisation avoids look-ahead bias but makes early values noisy; full-sample standardisation is look-ahead and is the more common error
sources: Hollo, Kremer & Lo Duca 2012, CISS: a composite indicator of systemic stress (ECB Working Paper 1426)
Kliesen, Owyang & Vermann 2012 (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis Review 94:369)

cards.method: Correlation-network filtering: minimum spanning tree and planar graphs
cards.when: a correlation matrix has too many edges to read; filtering to a sparse graph exposes the structure that matters
cards.when_not: the matrix is small enough to read directly; the correlations are estimated on too little data to be stable

alternatives.criterion: the sparsest connected representation
keeps more edges while staying readable
simplest, but threshold-dependent and can disconnect the graph

output_key_fields: graph: the filtered network
tree_length: total edge length, a market-state indicator
centrality: node importance in the filtered graph
stability: edge persistence across rolling windows
interpretation_traps: FILTERING DISCARDS INFORMATION BY DESIGN; the minimum spanning tree keeps only N-1 edges and the discarded ones are not noise by assumption
the tree is unstable when correlations are close together, so edges flip between windows without any economic change
correlation is not distance; the metric transformation used affects which edges survive
sources: Mantegna 1999 (European Physical Journal B 11:193-197)
Tumminello, Aste, Di Matteo & Mantegna 2005 (Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 102:10421)
networkx

arguments.name: l
arguments.description: Handle to a numeric vector of row sums (total LIABILITIES of each bank), length >= 2, non-negative, without NA/Inf; sum(l)==sum(a) is required.

arguments.name: a
arguments.description: Handle to a numeric vector of column sums (total ASSETS of each bank), same length as l, non-negative.

arguments.name: targetdensity
arguments.description: Target network density ∈ (0,1] (default 0.5).

arguments.name: seed
arguments.description: Reproducibility seed of the calibration (positive integer; default 1).

arguments.name: nsamples_calib
arguments.description: Number of matrices in the calibration (positive integer; default 100).

arguments.name: thin_calib
arguments.description: Thinning during the calibration (positive integer; default 100).

arguments.name: tol
arguments.description: Relative tolerance of the sum(l)==sum(a) balance check (default 1e-6).

arguments.name: exposures
arguments.description: Handle to a SQUARE (n x n) non-negative matrix of bilateral exposures (assets network: A->B => A has an asset in B); e.g. the exposure_matrix from nrm_reconstruct_matrix.

arguments.name: buffer
arguments.description: Handle to a numeric non-negative vector of capital buffer per node (length n).

arguments.name: weights
arguments.description: Handle to a non-negative vector of weights per node (e.g. total assets; length n, positive sum >0). Default: equal weights rep(1,n) — unweighted.

arguments.name: shock
arguments.description: "all" (default; one default scenario per node) or a JSON array of n percentage shocks in [0,1] (a single scenario).

arguments.name: method
arguments.description: 'debtrank' (Bardoscia et al. 2015 continuous stress propagation) or 'threshold' (traditional Furfine default cascades). Default 'debtrank'.

arguments.name: exposure_type
arguments.description: Matrix interpretation: 'assets' (A->B: A has an asset in B; default) or 'liabilities' (A->B: A owes B).

arguments.name: max_it
arguments.description: Maximum propagation iterations (default 1000).

arguments.name: single_hit
arguments.description: Only for method='debtrank': True => old single-hit DebtRank (Battiston et al. 2012). Default False.

arguments.name: rowsums
arguments.description: Handle to a numeric vector of ASSETS per node (row sums; length >= 2, non-negative); sum(rowsums) MUST == sum(colsums).

arguments.name: colsums
arguments.description: Handle to a numeric vector of LIABILITIES per node (column sums; same length as rowsums, non-negative, equal total sum).

arguments.name: method
arguments.description: Reconstruction method: 'me' Maximum Entropy (Upper & Worm 2004; dense, deterministic); 'md' Minimum Density (Anand et al. 2015; sparse, STOCHASTIC -> seed). Default 'me'.

arguments.name: seed
arguments.description: Positive integer seed for reproducibility of 'md' (default 1).

arguments.name: max_it
arguments.description: Maximum iterations (default 100000).

arguments.name: abs_tol
arguments.description: Convergence tolerance (default 0.001).

arguments.name: md_c
arguments.description: md: cost of an additional link (Anand et al.; default 1).

arguments.name: md_lambda
arguments.description: md: low-density fraction for the first md_k rounds, in [0,1] (default 1).

arguments.name: md_k
arguments.description: md: low-density allocation rounds (default 100).

arguments.name: md_theta
arguments.description: md: scaling parameter prior (default 1).

arguments.name: md_remove_prob
arguments.description: md: probability of randomly removing a link, in [0,1) (default 0.01).

arguments.name: l
arguments.description: Handle to row sums (liabilities); same as build_er_model.

arguments.name: a
arguments.description: Handle to col sums (assets); same length as l, sum(l)==sum(a).

arguments.name: model
arguments.description: Handle to a systemicrisk model (build_er_model.model).

arguments.name: nsamples
arguments.description: Number of posterior samples of matrix L (positive integer; default 100).

arguments.name: thin
arguments.description: Thinning: theta updates per sample (positive integer; default 100).

arguments.name: seed
arguments.description: Reproducibility seed of the MCMC (positive integer; default 1). REQUIRED determinism.

arguments.name: matrpertheta
arguments.description: Matrix updates per theta update (positive integer; default length(l)^2).

arguments.name: burnin
arguments.description: Number of burn-in iterations (positive integer; default auto).

arguments.name: probs
arguments.description: 2 increasing quantiles ∈ (0,1) for lower/upper matrices per cell (default [0.05, 0.95]).

arguments.name: tol
arguments.description: Relative tolerance of the sum(l)==sum(a) balance check (default 1e-6).

arguments.name: returns
arguments.description: Handle to a numeric matrix of daily returns; >= 3 columns; >= 90 rows (coarse pre-gate) AND >= 3 full calendar months (~>= 100 rows; post-gate n_months>=3, otherwise blocked-by-gate: with < 3 months the monthly min-max degenerates to {0,1}); without NA/NaN/Inf. All columns become network nodes.

arguments.name: seed
arguments.description: Seed (default 123) — stabilizes the eigenvector-centrality routine (ARPACK) for determinism.

arguments.name: returns
arguments.description: Handle to a numeric matrix of returns; column 1 = the system/market index, columns 2..p = institutions (>= 2 institutions, i.e. >= 3 columns); >= 30 rows; without NA/NaN/Inf. q=0.95 is hardcoded in the package.

arguments.name: returns
arguments.description: Handle to a numeric matrix of returns; column 1 = the system, columns 2..p = institutions (>= 3 columns); >= 50 rows; without NA/NaN/Inf.

arguments.name: state_variables
arguments.description: Handle to a numeric matrix of state variables (e.g. VIX, spreads); >= 2 columns (NSV=1 breaks the package); same number of rows as returns; without NA/NaN/Inf.

arguments.name: x
arguments.description: Handle to a numeric vector (>= 2 elements, non-constant, without NA/NaN/Inf); min-max into [0,1].
